EUPATRID: One well born, or of noble birth.

EXULT: To be in high spirits; figuratively, to leap for joy; to rejoice in triumph or exceedingly; to triumph; as, an exulting heart. "An exulting countenance." Bancroft. The dumb shall sing, the lame his crutch forego, And leap exulting like the bounding roe. Pope.
EMBED: To lay as in a bed; to lay in surrounding matter; to bed; as, to embed a thing in clay, mortar, or sand.

The expectancy and rose of the fair state. Shak. EMBRAVE: 1. To inspire with bravery. [Obs.] Beaumont. 2. To decorate; to make showy and fine. [Obs.] And with sad cypress seemly it embraves. Spenser.
EFFLUVIATE: To give forth effluvium. [R.] "An effluviating power." Boyle.
EQUILIBRIUM: 1. Equality of weight or force; an equipoise or a state of rest produced by the mutual counteraction of two or more forces. 2. EGYPTOLOGY: The science or study of Egyptian antiquities, esp. the hieroglyphics.
EXCHANGEABLE: 1. Capable of being exchanged; fit or proper to be exchanged. The officers captured with Burgoyne were exchangeable within the powers of General Howe. Marshall. 2. Available for making exchanges; ratable. "An exchangeable value." J. S. Mill.
EVERLIVING: 1. Living always; immoral; eternal; as, the everliving God. 2. Continual; incessant; unintermitted.
ENSCONCE: To cover or shelter, as with a sconce or fort; to place or hide securely; to conceal. She shall not see me: I will ensconce me behind the arras. Shak.
EXSUFFLATE: To exorcise or renounce by blowing.
EPICARDIAC: Of or relating to the epicardium.
ERYNGO: A plant of the genus Eryngium.

EDIFYING: Instructing; improving; as, an edifying conversation. -- Ed"i*fy`ing*ly, adv. -- Ed"i*fy`ing*ness, n.
EVIDENTIAL: Relating to, or affording, evidence; indicative; especially, relating to the evidences of Christianity. Bp. Fleetwood. "Evidential tracks." Earle.. -- Ev`i*den"tial*ly, adv.
ELAEIS: A genus of palms. Note: Elæis Guineensis, the African oil palm, is a tree twenty or thirty feet high, with immense pinnate leaves and large masses of fruit. The berries are rather larger than olives, and when boiled in water yield the orange-red palm oil.
ENAMELER: One who enamels; a workman or artist who applies enamels in ornamental work. [Written also enameller, enamellist.]
EPISEPALOUS: Growing on the sepals or adnate to them.
EURYALIDA: A tribe of Ophiuroidea, including the genera Euryale, Astrophyton, etc. They generally have the arms branched. See Astrophyton.
EXTROVERSION: The condition of being turned wrong side out; as, extroversion of the bladder. Dunglison.
ERUMPENT: Breaking out; -- said of certain fungi which burst through the texture of leaves.
EXCIPLE: The outer part of the fructification of most lichens.
EVACUATIVE: Serving of tending to evacuate; cathartic; purgative.
EDILESHIP: The office of ædile. T. Arnold.
EURITE: A compact feldspathic rock; felsite. See Felsite.

EXTIMULATION: Stimulation. [Obs.] Things insipid, and without any extimulation. Bacon.
ESERINE: An alkaloid found in the Calabar bean, and the seed of Physostigma venenosum; physostigmine. It is used in ophthalmic surgery for its effect in contracting the pupil.
EDITORIALLY: In the manner or character of an editor or of an editorial article.
ENLIVEN: 1. To give life, action, or motion to; to make vigorous or active; to excite; to quicken; as, fresh fuel enlivens a fire. Lo! of themselves th' enlivened chessmen move. Cowley. 2. ENROLLMENT: 1. The act of enrolling; registration. Holland. 2. A writing in which anything is enrolled; a register; a record. Sir J. Davies.
EPISCOPIZE: To make a bishop of by consecration. Southey. To perform the duties of a bishop.
EUPHEMISM: A figure in which a harts or indelicate word or expression is softened; a way of describing an offensive thing by an inoffensive expression; a mild name for something disagreeable.
EMPHYSEMA: A swelling produced by gas or air diffused in the cellular tissue. Emphysema of the lungs, Pulmonary emphysema (Med.), a common disease of the lungs in which the air cells are distended and their partition walls ruptured by an abnormal pressure of the air contained in them.
EXAGGERATE: 1. To heap up; to accumulate. [Obs.] "Earth exaggerated upon them [oaks and firs]." Sir M. Hale. 2. To amplify; to magnify; to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth ; to delineate extravagantly ; to overstate the truth concerning. A friend exaggerates a man's virtues. Addison.
ERIACH: A recompense formerly given by a murderer to the relatives of the murdered person.
ESCRITOIRE: A piece of furniture used as a writing table, commonly with drawers, pigeonholes, and the like; a secretary or writing desk.
ENUBILATE: To clear from mist, clouds, or obscurity. [R.] Bailey.
ERGOTISM: A logical deduction. [Obs.] Sir T. Browne. A diseased condition produced by eating rye affected with the ergot fungus.
ERYTHEMATIC: Characterized by, or causing, a morbid redness of the skin; relating to erythema.
EXPURGATORIAL: Tending or serving to expurgate; expurgatory. Milman.
EXPOUND: 1. To lay open; to expose to view; to examine. [Obs.] He expounded both his pockets. Hudibras. 2. To lay open the meaning of; to explain; to clear of obscurity; to interpret; as, to expound a text of Scripture, a law, a word, a meaning, or a riddle. Expound this matter more fully to me. Bunyan.
EXPELLER: One who. or that which, expels.

ENDOMORPH: A crystal of one species inclosed within one of another, as one of rutile inclosed in quartz.

EU: A prefix used frequently in composition, signifying well, good, advantageous; -- the opposite of dys-.
EGRIOT: A kind of sour cherry. Bacon.
EPEE: A sharp-pointed dueling sword without a cutting edge, used in fencing; crossword favorite.
